facts.value: Media freedom is a fundamental right that applies to all member states of the European Union and its citizens.
Media freedom is defined in the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights.
Media freedom is also defined in the European Convention on Human Rights.
Guaranteeing media freedom is named a key indicator of a country's readiness to become part of the EU.
Some EU-wide media focusing on European affairs have emerged since the early 1990s.
Examples of EU-wide media include Euronews, Eurosport, EUobserver, EURACTIV, and Politico Europe.
Arte is a public Franco-German TV network that promotes programming in the areas of culture and the arts.

80 percent of Arte's programming is provided in equal proportion by the two member companies, while the remainder is provided by the European Economic Interest Grouping ARTE GEIE and the channel's European partners.
The MEDIA Programme of the European Union has supported the European popular film and audiovisual industries since 1991.
The MEDIA Programme provides support for the development, promotion and distribution of European works within Europe and beyond.
